newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH C.BANK HEAD CALLS FOR LOWER 1997 DEFICIT.
newsitem.headline: POLISH C.BANK HEAD CALLS FOR LOWER 1997 DEFICIT.

text.p: The President of the National Bank of Poland Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz called on deputies on Thursday to keep next year's budget deficit as low as possible to help the economy maintain its positive momentum in 1997.

She said the 1997 budget's goals -- 5.5 percent growth of gross domestic product, year-on-year inflation at 13 percent compared with this year's expected 17.8 percent and a balanced current account -- required a gap of 2.3-2.4 percent of GDP.

"The unquestionable need to further reduce inflation in order to uphold econmic growth, investment and cut unemployment requires appropriate control of money supply growth," Gronkiewicz Waltz told the lower house at the start of the 1997 budget debate.

The government budget draft envisages cutting the budget gap to 2.6 percent of GDP next year from 2.8 percent this year, but the deficit may stay at 2.8 percent or even rise depending on the outcome of the ongoing debate of the 1997 tax levels.
Gronkiewicz-Waltz said a higher deficit would force the NBP to implement a more restrictive monetary policy if the government macroeconomic targets were to be achieved.
Otherwise inflation would have to be higher than 13 percent and currency reserves would fall, she said.

"If you approve a deficit which boosts money supply either by its size or the way it would be financed... you will vote for either a reduction of credit for the economy, higher inflation or for a deepening of the trade deficit which would lead to a drop in official currency reserves and which could diminish the credibility of Poland," she said .
"All three possiblities would not be good for Poland, so I call on you to vote for a budget which would minimise the financing of public spending through credit," she said.
Parliament has until January 28 to approve the 1997 budget. The tax bill, however, to become law in 1997, has to be out of parliament and signed by the president by the end of this month.
